independent.summary: The LEO-100 correction inserts a claim that is stale against the tree it was merged into: it says `weeklyDigestDue` "requires an exact UTC hour **and** weekday match (`services/weeklyDigest.js:66-67`)" and that the catch-up arm "is LEO-084's, out of scope", so "the earliest a rolled-back entity can send is its next weekly slot". Both were true only of the pre-LEO-084 file (cf22026:66-67 held the two `return false` guards); LEO-084 merged 2026-11-05 — two days before LEO-100 itself shipped (c4b744d, 11-07) — so in the shipped and current code the hour+weekday match lives at weeklyDigest.js:145, lines 66-67 are the MIN_GAP_MS comment, and `weeklyDigestDue` is `slot-match` OR `catch-up` once elapsed >= CATCHUP_MS (8d). A rollback restoring a ~7-day-old stamp therefore retries via the catch-up arm roughly a day after the missed slot, not a week later — i.e. the correction replaces one wrong statement in a spec body with another, which is the exact class of error this item exists to remove. No code impact (docs only), and the sentence is internally consistent with LEO-100's own as-filed out-of-scope line (1612), which is why this is low rather than higher.
